questions.question: Given the homogeneous state-space equaion [latex]\dot{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -3 &1 \\ 0&-2 \end{bmatrix}x[/latex] the steady state value [latex]x_{ss}=\lim_{t\rightarrow \infty }x(t)[/latex], given the initial state value of [latex]x\left ( t \right )=\left [ 10-10 \right ]^{T}[/latex], is
questions.explanation: [latex][sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &-1 \\ 0 & s+2 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} =\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} &\frac{1}{(s+2)(s+3)} \\ 0& \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0) =\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 10\\ -10 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 20e^{-3t}-10e^{-2t}\\ -10e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex] [latex]\therefore \;\; X_{ss}=\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty }\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex][sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} s+3 &-1 \\ 0 & s+2 \end{bmatrix}^{-1} =\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{s+3} &\frac{1}{(s+2)(s+3)} \\ 0& \frac{1}{s+2} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]e^{At}=L^{-1}[sI-A]^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]x(t)=e^{At}X(0) =\begin{bmatrix} e^{-3t} & e^{-2t}-e^{-3t}\\ 0 & e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 10\\ -10 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; x(t)=\begin{bmatrix} 20e^{-3t}-10e^{-2t}\\ -10e^{-2t} \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore \;\; X_{ss}=\lim_{t \rightarrow \infty }\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]

\phi  &= 113.178^{\circ}-90^{\circ} \\

\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question:
A half-wave thyristor converter supplies a purely inductive load, as shown in
figure. If the triggering angle of the thyristor is [latex]120^{\circ}[/latex], the extinction angle will
be
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} V_m \sin \omega t&=L\frac{di}{dt}\\ \frac{di}{dt}&=\frac{V_m}{L} \sin \omega t\\ \int_{0}^{i}di&=\frac{V_m}{L} \int_{\alpha }^{t}\sin \omega t\; dt\\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} \cos \omega t|_t^\alpha \\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \omega t)\;\;...(i)\\ \text{For extinction angle, at }&\omega t=\beta ,i=0\\ \Rightarrow \;0&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \beta )\\ \text{Which gives, }& \cos \alpha = \cos \beta \\ \beta &=2 n \pi \pm \alpha \\ \text{For, } n&=1\\ \beta &=240^{\circ},480^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html: [latex]\begin{aligned} V_m \sin \omega t&=L\frac{di}{dt}\\ \frac{di}{dt}&=\frac{V_m}{L} \sin \omega t\\ \int_{0}^{i}di&=\frac{V_m}{L} \int_{\alpha }^{t}\sin \omega t\; dt\\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} \cos \omega t|_t^\alpha \\ i&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \omega t)\;\;...(i)\\ \text{For extinction angle, at }&\omega t=\beta ,i=0\\ \Rightarrow \;0&=\frac{V_m}{\omega L} (\cos \alpha -\cos \beta )\\ \text{Which gives, }& \cos \alpha = \cos \beta \\ \beta &=2 n \pi \pm \alpha \\ \text{For, } n&=1\\ \beta &=240^{\circ},480^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
